### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ba5a2eed74f36111e6dc64494e0eeffbef6aafa` — the merge of head `084e79e1659a99bb77bfe015c654c0b57f9ebfb5` into base `ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ba5a2eed74f36111e6dc64494e0eeffbef6aafa && git checkout 4ba5a2eed74f36111e6dc64494e0eeffbef6aafa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1 084e79e1659a99bb77bfe015c654c0b57f9ebfb5 && git checkout -B drift-repro ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1 && git merge --no-ff 084e79e1659a99bb77bfe015c654c0b57f9ebfb5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ba4afcc2391922a86678bf5e47b1a0e4d2c87ff1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4746b38c1052cd0451448c07cc6df9bf69bbfa58`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/10757-request-rounds-core.md, .changeset/10757-request-rounds-metadata-protocol.md, content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx, content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.request-rounds.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-localization-cache.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/meta-overlay-cache.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/meta-overlay-cache.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.datasource-delete-prolongation.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.item-read-overlay-cache.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/objectql/src/write-epoch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`executeWithMiddleware`, `registerMiddleware`, `hasObjectMiddleware`, `transaction`, `insertMany`, the bound-object delegates), packages/core/src/security/resolve-user-grants-cache.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-grants-memo.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/overlay-index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/recorded-by-sentinel.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/package.json, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`enforceApiAccess`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (the `customSession` call, the `ai_access` note), packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts, scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs

Inputs: card #10757 (body and all 17 comments, the ruling 6250819728, the reading 6255731843, the release 6255757782, the retriage 6256237052, the claim 6264940865, the dispatch 6264971259, the leg-A note 6265900988, the `os-dev-report` 6267599450 read as claims), #11633 (the design 5394942824 §4 leg C/D and Forks 3–4, the acceptance 5404681591), #11967 (the leg-D report 5440580595 and its ACCEPT), #15194's territory declaration 6264887348 and the two rulings after it (6266750393, 6267391172 — neither answers the declaration), #24515 (closed `not_planned` at 6265874149), PR #24533's body, 13-file list and the net diff against merge base `f4755a68a7` (+1218/−211), and the head's check-runs read twice (12:57Z and 13:06Z).

### ① Derived judgments

**Leg 5 — the localization cache's retirement set is exactly the set of writes that can change its answer. Right.**
- What the answer is read from: `SettingsService.loadRows` reads the global rung from `sys_platform_setting` (`settings-service.ts:81`, `PLATFORM_SETTING_OBJECT`) and the tenant and user rungs from `sys_setting` (`:58`, `DEFAULT_OBJECT`); the resolver's direct fallback reads `sys_setting` through `ql.find`. The manifest defaults and `OS_LOCALIZATION_*` are process state. So `LOCALIZATION_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS = {sys_setting, sys_platform_setting}` is complete.
- Every in-process writer of those two tables goes through the engine: the settings service writes with `this.engine.update(object, …)` / `this.engine.insert(object, …)` (`settings-service.ts:2957`, `:2981`) and emits `emitChange` (`:773`, `:2223`, the primary seam, unchanged); seeds write through `this.engine.insert/update` (`seed-loader.ts:1149–1181`, `:2630–2675`). A repo-wide search of non-test code finds no raw SQL or knex write to either table; the one raw handle on `sys_setting` is `packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts:313`, a `find`, in a CLI process this cache cannot see anyway (the peer-write case, TTL-bounded, unchanged from before).
- The seam fires for every engine write verb: `insert`, `update`, `delete` each run `executeWithMiddleware` (`engine.ts:15469`, `:16873`, `:19697`); `insertMany` is `this.insert(object, rows, …)` (`:16576`); the bound-object API delegates to `engine.insert/update/delete` (`:21616–21660`); there is no `upsert`. An unkeyed registration is in `applicable` for every object (`:6627–6629`) and is not counted by `hasObjectMiddleware` (`:6602`), as the new pin asserts. Any non-read verb on a watched object, including one the list has never heard of, retires (the read set is `find`/`findOne`/`count`/`aggregate`), the safe direction. The non-`write` reasons (`remote`, `metadata`, `manual`) retire wholesale through `writeEpoch.subscribe` — the same two-seam shape `resolve-user-grants-cache.ts:196–236` landed for leg B.
- The failure entry keeps its TTL-only rule (`localizationEntryIsLive` returns `true` for `kind === 'failure'`), pinned.
- Timing: the generation is read before the resolve and stored with the entry; the middleware bumps in `finally` after `next()` settles, so an in-flight resolve across a write stamps the pre-write generation and is dead on arrival (pinned, "the retirement lands AFTER the write settles").

**Leg 6 — the overlay cache's retirement set. Right, with one residual window named below (TTL-bounded, not a bypass, and narrower than before).**
- The cached value is the raw `sys_metadata` row set and nothing else, for the list read and the by-name read alike. Every writer of `sys_metadata` in server code goes through the engine: `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1168` (update), `:1177` (insert), `:1323` (delete), `protocol.ts:31072` (delete), the seed loader's `this.engine.insert/update`. The two `migrations/*` files are DDL (overlay-index) or a `sys_metadata_history` update (recorded-by-sentinel). The only raw handle, `packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts:559`, is a `driver.find` in a CLI process. No raw SQL writer exists.
- Writes whose visible effect comes from another source: a package's disabled flag and the artifact table are registry/in-memory state consulted on every call (`getMetaItem` runs `isObjectOfDisabledPackage` before `readMetaItem`; `readMetaItem` merges layers per call); `sys_metadata_activation` feeds the grants envelope (leg B's watched set), not this row set. Package install/uninstall/publish change `sys_metadata` rows through the repository, so they retire. A peer's write arrives as `applyRemoteMetadataMutation` → `bumpWriteEpoch(this.engine, 'remote')` (`protocol.ts:8143`) → the subscribe listener bumps the generation; pinned by the prolongation suite's ablation. `metadata.changed` still does not retire it — unchanged since #11967 (5440580595 refuted that channel), and the docs page now says so correctly.
- **Residual window, stated exactly:** `SysMetadataRepository.put` and `delete` run inside `withTxn` → `engine.transaction` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:685–693`, `:1069`, `:1285`), writing the `sys_metadata` row and then the `sys_metadata_history` row in one transaction. The middleware bumps the generation when the `sys_metadata` operation settles — before the history insert and before commit. A `/data` request whose by-name read starts in that window reads the pre-commit row on another connection and stamps the new generation, so `enforceApiAccess` can hold a pre-publish `enable` for that one object until the TTL (30 s) or the next `sys_metadata` write. This is not a missed write path: the write passes the seam; the seam fires before commit. The same window existed for the list read since #11967, wider (the epoch bumped at operation START, `engine.ts:6623`), so for the list read this PR narrows it; for the by-name read it is new only in that the read is cached at all, which the retriage ordered, and the design's rule (#11633 §0: seam plus TTL bound) covers it. The window is one history-insert round trip wide. Judged acceptable; the docs prose should say "commits" where it says "settles" (see ②).
- Pre-registration write in flight: stated in both docblocks and the PR body; the epoch reading it replaced was blind to it too; TTL-bounded.

**Leg 6's by-name coverage — byte-identical for every caller. Right.** `readItemActiveRows(type, name, cached = false)` is uncached for every caller except `getMetaItem` → `readMetaItem(request, { servedRead: true })` → `readItemActiveRows(…, true)`, and only when `readState === 'active'` (`protocol.ts:11309`, `:11444`); draft and `previewDrafts` reads are untouched. The hit is a `structuredClone` of rows cloned on store, upstream of the parse, the package-less binding, the served-row selection and the lock, which all run per call. The authoring read is pinned to keep reading the store. An engine without both seams, or TTL `0`, declines (pinned; `rest-data-read-one-overlay-read.test.ts`'s epoch-less engine keeps its multiset). The key spells the by-name entry `['item', type, packageId, name]` so it never collides with the list entry. The cache is keyed per engine; `findEnvironmentRows` adds no environment column (the environment is the engine's database, ADR-0131 D6), so the per-engine key is sound.

**Leg 4 — the merged wave. Right; the envelope and the C8 regions are byte-identical.**
- The old ledger question was the names of `applyingGrants` (`grantAppliesInTenant(org, tenant) || anchorsPlatformStanding(r)`); the new one is the names where `mayApply` (`grantAppliesInTenant || (anchorReadsDefaultOrganization && name === admin_full_access && org !== null)`). Proof the new set contains the old: `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` (`:912–922`) is true only when not walled and either `org === null` — then `grantAppliesInTenant(null, …)` is true (`:861`: `!organizationId || …`) — or `org === defaultOrganizationId !== undefined`, which implies `anchorReadsDefaultOrganization` and `org !== null`. So no name the old code asked is dropped, and the only addition is `admin_full_access` for an organization-owned grant that turns out not to anchor.
- Nobody reads the extra verdict: `disabled.permissions` is consumed only as `.has(name)` for names in `applyingGrants` and `boundSetNames` (`:1610–1640`), `disabled.positions` only filters `grants.positions`; no later reader exists (checked past `:1700`). `hasPlatformAdminGrant` derives from `anchorsPlatformStanding(grant) && active` as before; the deactivated-anchor case is pinned.
- The widening is a predicate move on the activation-ledger read in that one case: `name IN` gains one name and `limit` (`names.length * 2`, `:1000`) grows by 2. It is disclosed in the PR body, the changeset, the deviations and the pin (`ledgerReadOf([... ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS])`). The PR body's "the filter shape is byte-identical" is loose; the same sentence states the widening, so the record is honest.
- The C8 regions named in 6264887348 are untouched: the diff's hunks in `resolve-authz-context.ts` are `:1495–1600` and `:1913` onward; `grantAppliesInTenant` (`:861`), `grantOrganizationOf` (`:890`), `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` (`:912`) and `readDefaultOrganizationId` (`:934`, `{ slug: 'default' }` limit 1) are outside them, and the organization read is pinned byte-for-byte in all five cases. Error direction: `Promise.all` rejects if either read throws; the sequential version threw too (fail closed, unchanged).

**The cold leg — the `attachedHere` guard is load-bearing. Right, and rightly ruled out.** `withRequestGrantsMemo` registers the observer at scope open (`request-grants-memo.ts:235–236`) and `commit` stores nothing for an engine this scope attached (`:318`). The engine snapshots `applicable` when an operation starts (`engine.ts:6627`), so a write in flight at registration never passes the observer, and its epoch bump already happened at its start (`:6623`), so `epochAtOpen === epochNow` and `started === completed` would both hold across it: without the guard a revocation landing between the first request's two resolutions is served stale. The dev's one-shot reading (guard removed → `auditor` served) matches this reading of the code. The only whole fix is registering the observer before the first request — a boot seam outside the fence; the dev's option A (leave it, once per process, 7 queries / 2 rounds) is the sound one.

**The duplicate `sys_user` read, ruled out to `plugin-auth`. Right.** Row 2 is better-auth's `handleFallbackJoin` through plugin-auth's adapter; row 3 is `getUserRow` (`resolve-authz-context.ts:1318`, memoized within one resolution) inside `resolveUserAuthzGrants` as called from the `customSession` callback (`auth-manager.ts:4515`). better-auth's user deliberately omits `ai_access` (`auth-manager.ts:1747`), which `getUserRow` is read for (`:1723`), so one read can serve both only through a plugin-auth seed. Both reads sit in wave 1, so removing one saves a query and no round — no measured pull for a core option nothing passes.

**The re-reading against the retriage's target. Done-when met; `Fixes #10757` is right.** Retriage 6256237052's done-when: each item landed or ruled out with its reading, plus one local re-reading by 6255731843's method posted on the card. Leg A: ruled out with its reading (6265874149, carried at 6265900988, which corrects the expected floor to count leg A as 2 rounds). Leg 4: the wave landed and pinned; the duplicate read ruled out with its reading. Leg 5 and leg 6: landed and pinned. Cold: ruled out with its reading. The re-reading is posted at 6267599450 (method, trees, controls, per-query table): opt-ins on 3 / 3, the corrected floor; stock 11 / 6 admin and 10 / 6 member, from 12 / 8 and 11 / 7; after an unrelated write 0 of 6 retirements, from 6 of 6. The dispatch's "Part of" was conditioned on leg A landing; leg A was ruled out instead, which the done-when accepts, so the seat's patch to `Fixes` is right. The ruling's bounds hold: no claim about cloud#1521 or cloud#1518 is made; the stock default still pays 6 rounds and the PR says so.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/core` patch and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and both changesets — right.
- No accept set, served body or authz answer moves: the resolved envelope and the served bodies are unchanged by construction (above) and by the dev's controls.
- No public surface moves. `meta-overlay-cache.ts` is not re-exported from `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` and the package's `exports` map has only `"."`, so `readOverlayCacheGeneration`, `META_OVERLAY_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS` and the new `name` key field are package-internal. In core, `LOCALIZATION_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS`, `localizationWriteState` and `LocalizationWriteState` are module-private; `resolveLocalizationContext` (exported at `security/index.ts:213`) and `resolveUserAuthzGrants` keep their signatures. `readItemActiveRows` and `readMetaItem` are private and gained defaulted parameters. The two env vars keep their names, defaults and parsing (malformed → off).
- The internal `WriteEpochSeam` now requires `subscribe`; a real engine's `WriteEpoch` has it, and a double without it declines rather than caching — the stricter direction, pinned.
- Docs prose against code: `environment-variables.mdx` and `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` state the new rule (watched-table write, non-`write` bump, TTL; a write to any other object does not retire) and match the code. One looseness to carry: "retires the entry once the write settles and before the next read" / "read-your-writes is exact on the node that made the write" is exact for a read that starts after the transaction commits; a concurrent request's read in the settle-to-commit window of a transactional publish can cache the pre-commit row for the TTL (①, leg 6). Acceptance-note material, not a changeset error.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Fence widened to the list read's retirement, the two docs pages and the ledger.** Accepted. (a) Narrowing the list read's trigger is the same module as the by-name coverage, is the trigger #11633 §4 leg D names ("any engine-seam write to `sys_metadata`"), and without it the measured by-name cache was retired by every data write (leg456 run: 12 / 7 after each forced write). (b) Two hand-written docs pages stated the old rule; correcting them is owed, and neither is release-owned. (c) `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` was written by the gate's own `--write` for a double the new suite exercises; the head's "Lint · CI, release & engine gates" check is green.
- **The `admin_full_access` name.** The dispatch's "no predicate change" is read against the territory declaration's named regions: `grantAppliesInTenant`, `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` and the organization read's filter are byte-identical and pinned. The moved predicate is the activation-ledger read's `name IN` list and derived `limit`, in one case, read by no verdict, disclosed four ways. Answered as a declared deviation, not a breach of the C8 territory. Open: the epic seat has not answered 6264887348 (its two later comments on #15194 are 18.x-line rulings). The dispatch owes "an objection-free read of this thread" before the queue; that is the dispatching seat's act, not this record's.
- **Six pushes.** All to the one branch; AGENTS.md requires a WIP push before every minutes-long step, and the claim set no push budget. No flag.
- **Dist-only instrumentation and the `check-dev-prereqs` hand-stamp.** A measurement deviation, disclosed: sources edited, built, reverted blob-equal, dists rebuilt clean; `scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs:153–157` names the hand-run `--stamp` as the class its artifact-side check cannot see. The diff carries no instrumentation (13 files, none under `packages/drivers`), and no gate verdict rests on the instrumented dist. The readings are the dev's self-report; the pins and the head's check-runs are the verdicts this record rests on.
- **The first 70 families at the merge commit `bc343e9b9`, not the head.** The head differs from it by the ledger JSON and two docs pages; the gate verdicts are the head's own check-runs: at 13:06Z, 36 success, 7 skipped, 4 still running — `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`. `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core (2/6)` and `Test Core (6/6)` completed green between the two reads. The queue needs every check green; this record does not stand in for the four running ones.
- **`open_questions` answered.** Cold prime: A (leave it) — a boot-time cross-package call for a once-per-process saving earns no seam; a forgotten prime degrades to today's safe path. Duplicate `sys_user` carrier: the reading is right that it is plugin-auth's; it saves a query and no round, so no card is owed until a measured pull exists — carrier none stands. List read's retirement: A (keep) — the accepted design's trigger; the `remote` bump is pinned.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` judged.** (1) The duplicate `sys_user` read: no filing gate met (one query, zero rounds, carrier closed). (2) The cold double resolution: once per process, ruled load-bearing here; no filing gate met. (3) `rest-data-read-one-overlay-read.test.ts`'s header "nothing is kept between requests" now describes only its seam-less double: a stale test comment, acceptance-note material, no card.
- **Noted for the acceptance notes, not raised by the dev:** the settle-to-commit window on a transactional `sys_metadata` publish (①, leg 6) — bounded by the TTL, narrower than the epoch design it replaces, and the one place the docs' "settles" should read "commits".

## Delta note on record 6268067889

Head: `084e79e1659a99bb77bfe015c654c0b57f9ebfb5`. Written in-seat; local runs: none.

This note covers one commit on top of the record's head (`084e79e16`, parent `4746b38c1`), with no merge of `main`. It touches four files, +29/−13: two test files and two docs pages. No source file moved, so every judgment of record 6268067889 ①–③ carries over unchanged, and so does its **PASS**.

Inputs:
- the fix-round report 6269271222, read as claims;
- the commit's diff, read with `git diff` on fetched refs.

**The red, `Test Core (5/6)` (note 6268090803):** fixed at the cause.
- `storeEnvironmentRow` in `environment-overlay-five-types.test.ts` now writes its row through `engine.insert(…, { context: { isSystem: true } })`, not `driver.create`. It writes the same row shape as before: no organization, no package, the body as JSON, active, version 1.
- There is still no metadata write door in front of the row, and the control read still comes first. So the leg still asks the read alone. Its write now passes the `sys_metadata` seam that every production writer passes.
- No cache was disabled, no TTL changed and no assertion was weakened. The dev's before/after: exit 1 with 10 failed, then 26 / 26.

**The sweep:** the dev covered tests that write `sys_metadata`, `sys_setting` or `sys_platform_setting` straight into a driver. Each one named is either seeded before the stack boots or before its first served read, or it reads through a loader the new caches do not serve. Accepted as the premise sweep the fix round asked for.

**The record's two notes:**
- **The rest pin's header** now says why "nothing is kept between requests" holds only on its seam-less engine, and names where the real engine's retirement is pinned. Done.
